newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Nedlloyd still in rough seas.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Nedlloyd still in rough seas.

text.p: Dutch shipping and road transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV on Wednesday reported a 38 percent drop in third quarter profit and offered little prospect of improvement in the final quarter.

"Taking into account that the fourth quarter is generally weak for Nedlloyd, we expect Nedlloyd as a whole to end the year with a modestly positive result on ordinary activities after taxation," the company said.
But the net profit figure disguised some improvement for the firn. Ignoring capital gains on assets sold in 1995, ordinary net profit hit 36 million guilders ($21 million)from 19 million.
This growth was most marked in the Ocean Shipping sector, which saw improved volumes, cost reductions and a firmer dollar.
The capital gains in the third quarter of 1995 masked an improvement of 27 million guilders in shipping.
However, the upward trend is threatened by pressure on shipping freight rates which, the company said, would erode much of the anticipated gains from cost reductions.
Nedlloyd's European and Transport division had an unchanged operating profit in the third quarter of 23 million guilders.
The Unitrans operation in Germany continued to improve as expected, but Van Gend en Los in the Netherlands suffered from start-up costs of a new terminal in Eindhoven.
Nedlloyd was also unable to rely on the profitable Neddrill unit, which was sold to Noble Drilling NDCO.O in the second quarter.
Last year, Neddrill contributed eight million guilders in the third quarter, but the proceeds of the sale were used to reduce debt.
Nedlloyd shares sagged on the news, ending down 1.60 guilders at 44.20, compared with a year-high of 47.50 soon after the opening.
The net profit figure was at the top end of analysts' expectations, but it brought little exuberance.

"The bottom line was higher than I had been expecting. (Next year) may be worse and 1998 may be the bottom of the cycle. Container shipping is not a (good) business to be in. I have a neutral opinion on the company. I am probably going to switch to sell again. But I haven't decided about that," said Oscar Poos of Paribas Capital Markets.

"The net is a little above expectations, but the future looks mediocre to me. They repeat they expect 1996 results to be modestly positive, so the fourth quarter will be less good... It all depends on how the cooperation with P&O will work out," said Roel Gooskens, analyst at Van Meer James Capel.
The merger of Nedlloyd's container business with Peninsular and Orient, formalised last week, is yet to affect the bottom line. Analysts said it would need to produce significant economies of scale.
